scope: Proposition I.6 (Globalization in a fixed group) of the manuscript “Quasipolynomial Bounds for Arithmetic Progressions” (preprints/Quasipolynomial-Bounds-for-Arithmetic-Progressions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 159 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 481eaf7730dc4d58), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 183-184. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume Properties 1 and 2 of Proposition F.2, including its rank hypothesis and order of later parameter choices, the uniform symbol step-drop and separation statements, and their stated polynomial logarithmic bounds. Fix an early budget p and a strong rational projection π : G0 → Y of degree r ≤ s. Include the dimensions, rational structure constants, filtration bases, lattice grids, and matrix of π in the early complexity budget. Let PY (u, b) 183 be a weighted filtered polynomial, with no coefficient bound. Let Φu : G0/Γ0 → [0, 1] have an early uniform Lipschitz bound. Assume that, at each requested early accuracy η, the family {Φu} has a supremum-norm η-net of at most exp(P(p + log(1/η))) functions. Its bins may be arbitrary site sets. Let a(u) be a fixed real input of early bounded supremum. There are early output bounds, independent of every later sampling parameter, with the following consequence. Suppose a fraction at least e−p of paths have a permitted slice and a filtered polynomial gψ satisfying π(gψ(t)) = PY (ψ(t), β(ψ(t))), Eta(ψ(t))Φψ(t)(gψ(t)Γ0 ) ≥ e−p . Then there is one weighted filtered polynomial gU (u, b) in the same group, satisfying the formal identity πgU = PY , such that an early fraction of the original productive paths have permitted subslices on which replacement by gU gives early positive score. No coefficient bound on gψ or gU is required.
